scope.built: a slit spectrograph with a constant-width Gaussian line-spread function (resolving power stated at a reference wavelength), a polynomial truth wavelength solution, pixel-integrated spectra of a synthetic template (a blackbody continuum with Gaussian absorption lines, or an emission-line arc lamp) with photon and read noise, a pixel-integrated Gaussian line fit through js/inference/fit.js, a wavelength solution from marked arc lines through js/numeric/polyfit.js (Prompt 152) with residuals, covariance and Prompt 150's not-constrained state, a radial velocity with its uncertainty and the air/vacuum rule from the radiation line table (Prompt 125), a long-slit throughput and a line signal-to-noise with the resolving-power trade, one panel, one investigation at three depths
scope.notBuilt: a constant-R (prism) instrument, echelle orders and their overlap, a Voigt or Lorentzian line-spread function, a position-dependent line-spread function, flat fielding and fringing, sky subtraction, cosmic rays, slit tilt and curvature, spectral extraction, fibre fed spectrographs, atmospheric dispersion, telluric absorption, a real arc-lamp atlas (the lamp is synthetic, its lines the radiation line pack's NIST lines in air and vacuum with invented relative intensities), line identification by pattern matching, a facility spectrograph (Prompt 209's library has none and nothing is typed from memory), a measured arc from an archive (E1 uses SDSS stellar spectra already in the repository, no download)

reference.isolatedRule: a lamp line is isolated when every other lamp line is farther than 6 FWHM (1.8 nm) away, so that no neighbour reaches the 12-pixel fit window (amendment AM2; it was 2.5 FWHM); a pair closer than 2.5 FWHM (0.75 nm) is a blend (the pack's Ca II H / H-epsilon, the Mg b4 / b2 pair and the Na D pair are such pairs); the lamp's H-alpha (656.279 nm) lies outside the detector's 380 to 595 nm, so 22 of the 23 lamp lines fall on it

an emission line of total flux F on a zero continuum, pixel-integrated, sums over plus and minus 10 sigma to F to a relative 1e-12 at samplings of 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 pixels per FWHM (the convolution and the pixel integral conserve flux), and a pixel containing the line centre has the closed-form area

claimRule.intent: The resolving power is set by the line-spread function, not by the pixel size or the number of pixels: finer sampling does not separate two lines the line-spread function has merged. A wavelength solution is a fit with an uncertainty, the number of lines limits the degree, and a velocity needs the rest wavelength in the same medium as the observed one. No lesson text says finer pixels raise the resolving power, that two lines become one for lack of pixels alone, or that a velocity is read without the medium.

badControls: Smaller pixels raise the resolving power.
The resolving power is the number of pixels.
A cubic solution needs only three lines.
The air wavelength can be compared with a vacuum spectrum directly.
Los píxeles más pequeños aumentan el poder de resolución.
El poder de resolución es el número de píxeles.
Una solución cúbica necesita solo tres líneas.
permittedControls: Finer pixels sample the line better, but they cannot separate two lines the line-spread function has merged.
A cubic solution has four coefficients, so it needs at least four lines, and at least five to test itself.
A velocity needs the rest wavelength in the same medium, air or vacuum, as the observed one.
Los píxeles más finos muestrean mejor la línea, pero no separan dos líneas que la función de dispersión ya fundió.
